history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V39 workload, representation, width, job count, checksum, execution mode, scored operation, attribution counter, mixed-tier replay signature, timing boundary, occupancy rule, binary-provenance profile, and publication ruling. It changes no scored row or production engine behavior. It versions the tier-attribution sidecar from schema 13 to 14, updates its fail-closed validator, and re-pins the zig-js comparison runner after #974 added a separate diagnostic schema-v3 owned-memory inventory to attribution rows. Any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric source, adapter, integration ruling, diagnostic schema, or publication change needs its own version.
change: Re-pins bench/comparison_zig_js.zig after #974 added the Context memory inventory to each configuration, warmup, and invocation attribution row. The nested schema-v3 record reconciles exclusive Context backing, collector auxiliary scratch, recovery reserve, owned native mappings, and fixed controls; reports shared native code separately; and exposes non-additive logical heap, generation, and budget views. It is diagnostic only. Every representative workload, job count, checksum, timing boundary, scored attribution counter, mixed-tier allocation replay signature, occupancy rule, provenance check, and publication threshold is unchanged.

memory_inventory_diagnostics.reconciliation: accounted_owned_current_bytes equals Context backing plus collector auxiliary scratch plus external controls plus owned live and retired native mappings; external controls exactly partition into profiler, budget, serialized allocator, and recovery-reserve bytes
memory_inventory_diagnostics.publication_boundary: Memory inventory values are diagnostic machine-readable observations. They do not enter elapsed-time scores, exact allocation replay signatures, performance ratios, stability decisions, or publication acceptance.

exact_parent_integration.publication_boundary: V40 preserves every V39 timing, efficiency, cleanliness, checksum, serial-child, process-classification, provenance, and mixed-tier allocation-replay gate. The tier-attribution sidecar advances to schema 14 solely for schema-v3 memory inventory records, which remain diagnostic and retain a separate non-scored evidence boundary.

context_lifecycle_integration.publication_boundary: V40 changes only the shared runner hash. Lifecycle scenarios, options, checksums, phase and finalizer reconciliation, plateau policy, measured-boundary occupancy, and evidence ruling are unchanged.

no_jit_integration.publication_boundary: V40 changes only the shared runner hash. Required-bytecode and no-native modes, logical work, checksums, scored attribution, quickening contracts, publication duration, and exact-parent requirements are unchanged.

string_indexing_integration.publication_boundary: V40 changes only the shared runner hash. Every string representation, width, job count, checksum, required-bytecode boundary, scored attribution value, measured-boundary occupancy rule, and exact allocation replay remains unchanged.
